propositions: A model class configured with provider='bedrock' and a versioned canonical Bedrock id (containing a colon in the version suffix) silently discards the configured provider because _resolve_target treats any colon as a provider separator

The unqualified model string is then read back as 'provider:model' on its first colon, causing infer_provider to return only a fragment of the model id, leading to an 'unknown provider' error that contradicts the operator's explicit configuration

_resolve_target and infer_provider were two independent implementations of the same colon-based qualification test, allowing them to fail identically when the colon was in the model id rather than a separator

The fix consolidates the qualifier test into split_provider_qualifier using a regex pattern that validates provider-name format (lowercase identifier), and implements guard-order checking where an explicitly configured provider short-circuits the scan before any model string analysis

An already-qualified string like 'bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0' must not be double-prefixed, and conflicting configured-provider and inline-qualifier pairs must raise LLMConfigError rather than silently drop an explicit instruction
Versioned Bedrock aliases (canonical form with v1:0 suffix) must resolve correctly while unversioned aliases and existing unqualified values remain unchanged for back-compatibility
